topic: decisive: the installed simulator cannot discriminate kernel variants that differ 12 percent on hardware

cross_validation.pair: v23 (four accumulation chains, 16 inner iterations) vs v28 (eight chains, 8 inner iterations)

device_truth.difference: v28 is about 12 percent slower on the real device

reading: the two kernels issue the same total number of instructions (64 loads and 64 fma per row either way), so identical instruction counts are expected
but their hardware times differ by 12 percent because the dependency-chain depth and register pressure differ, and the simulator reports identical duration and identical total cycles
a model whose cycle count does not move for a change that costs 12 percent on the device cannot rank optimisations, so it cannot locate the bottleneck

why.correct_model_missing: there is no model directory for Ascend950PR_9579, the exact chip npu-smi reports, so the run falls back to the generic dav_3510 v100 model
why.populated_models_fail: the populated Ascend950PR_9571 and 9572 models both abort at aclInit with error 507000 on this host
other_limitations: code_exe.csv is empty because the aibin has no debug_line, so code-region attribution is unavailable
MTE2 appears as one instruction while the device reports DMA busy 27 percent (this model) to 86-93 percent (full kernel), so memory-bound behaviour is not represented

mission_impact: the hope that simulation could locate the prefill bottleneck is not supported by this installation; the device-side paired gate remains the only trustworthy instrument
